scope: High-priority claim-level evidence for THC-ENC-098 carbon-dioxide supply/enrichment context and THC-ENC-111 photoinhibition/high-light stress.
rules: Cannabis CO2 and high-light responses remain bounded to tested genotypes, environments, treatment ranges, measurement methods, and study duration.
NIOSH occupational exposure limits are worker-safety controls, not cultivation targets or system-design setpoints.
High-light studies support measured response within their tested ranges and do not establish a universal cannabis photoinhibition or injury threshold.
All mappings remain pending independent science review and do not alter lesson publication or independent-approval state.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Cannabis leaf gas exchange can respond to elevated CO2 under tested conditions, while occupational CO2 exposure limits and IDLH values are separate worker-safety controls that must not be treated as crop setpoints.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Chandra et al. (2011), DOI 10.1007/s12298-011-0066-6; NIOSH Pocket Guide to Chemical Hazards: Carbon Dioxide.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson's separation of measured crop response from facility life-safety limits and its warning against treating enrichment targets as safety limits.
claimEvidence.limitations: The cannabis study measured four varieties and defined CO2 treatments at leaf-gas-exchange scale; it does not establish universal yield, quality, enrichment, distribution, or economic targets. NIOSH limits do not design a cultivation control system.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Indoor cannabis can maintain increasing photosynthetic or yield responses across high tested PPFD ranges, but those experiments do not establish a universal no-injury or photoinhibition threshold across genotypes, environments, spectra, acclimation histories, and support conditions.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Rodriguez-Morrison, Llewellyn, and Zheng (2021), DOI 10.3389/fpls.2021.646020; Llewellyn et al. (2022), DOI 10.3389/fpls.2022.974018.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson's requirement to diagnose high-light stress with mapped exposure and plant/environment context rather than a single universal PPFD ceiling.
claimEvidence.limitations: Both studies used specific indoor genotypes, fixtures, environments, and treatment ranges; neither alone validates a universal photoinhibition threshold or visual diagnosis.
